attrs.evidence: nest_forgeries.mjs case a-verdict-token-is-not-a-verdict-VERIFIED-at-two-policies-is-two-facts (TRVM-P0.1): ONE artifact, FOUR verifiers. The liar table and a table differing only in checker_id both return verdict === VERIFIED with equal tokens, while their child_protocol_set_id and verifier_policy_id both differ; the honest table REFUSES the same bytes transitively through the alien checker; no table at all REFUSES and reports no child_protocol_set and the shipped policy id; and the coordinate is deterministic across calls, so it is a function of the SET and not of the call. Normative home: TRVM-NESTED-COMPOSITION-v2.md section 4.3 (both preimages), 6.2.1 (the table belongs to the verifier) and the section 8 bullet 'Not a verdict independent of who checked it'. Gate `gov-nest`, NEST-FORGERIES 44/44. Companion codes from the same round: nest-child-protocol-override-refused and nest-child-protocol-registration-malformed, which TRVM-P0 had folded into nest-policy-weakened because the vocabulary is release-pinned -- closed by spec revision 2 rather than by loosening spec_agreement.
attrs.statement: A VERDICT TOKEN IS NOT A VERDICT. VERIFICATION WITHOUT VERIFIER IDENTITY IS INCOMPLETE EVIDENCE. TRVM-P0 let a verifier EXTEND its protocol-to-checker table with checkers for protocols it does not implement, which is sound because the extension point belongs to the verifier and never to the artifact -- an artifact cannot name or inject checker code, a built-in cannot be replaced, and the parent still recomputes the certificate from the resolved child and compares it field by field. But it made the string VERIFIED ambiguous: the SAME artifact and store, judged under two supplied tables that differ ONLY in a checker_id, both answer VERIFIED, and under the honest table or no table at all the same bytes are REFUSED. A consumer that stores the token alone has stored a string that four different verifiers would have written differently. So the checker MUST report verifier_policy_id and, when a table was supplied, child_protocol_set_id and the effective set, and a consumer MUST NOT equate two verdicts because the token matches. THE COORDINATE IS NOT A LABEL: child_protocol_set_id is folded into the preimage of verifier_policy_id, so ONE identity names both what was bounded and who was allowed to check, and a verifier holding no table reports an id byte-identical to every id issued before the table existed. A checker_id is a NAME, not a warrant.
